openQuestions.question: Does a page the person controls on a personal domain (homepage, CV or résumé) count as “another authored text” that identifies the author?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, when the page is headed with the person’s name and lists the document by title; record it as the person’s own statement, not independent verification. 17 of the 31 proposals rest on such pages; one on a business-school faculty profile.

openQuestions.question: Does the publisher’s or employer’s own publication page (Meta for LLaMA, Google Research for batch normalisation and Concrete Problems) count as an institutional page?
openQuestions.recommended: Accept it as an institutional page, but label it as not independent of the byline: it confirms the institution credits the name, not who the person is. If the maintainer wants independence, hold these 13 records.

openQuestions.question: Initial-compatible forms (Michael I. Jordan / Michael Jordan / M. I. Jordan; MIRI’s “A Critch”).
openQuestions.recommended: Hold until a page prints the full name with the document; do not merge forms on the matching rule alone.

openQuestions.question: Usenet and mailing-list senders (Gudeman, Franzen, McCullough, Sandberg, Finney, Atkins) and pen names (Scott Alexander).
openQuestions.recommended: Keep as printed names. Propose a record only where the person’s own page or a later signed text claims the message; for a pen name, only with the maintainer’s decision on recording pen names as persons.

openQuestions.question: Later copies of the same document on an institution’s site (MIT economics hosting Andrews and Farboodi’s paper).
openQuestions.recommended: Do not count a copy of the document as identification; it repeats the byline.

openQuestions.question: Shortened titles on identifying pages (Jacob Hilton lists “InstructGPT” linking to arXiv 2203.02155).
openQuestions.recommended: Accept when the entry links the dataset’s expression; the note records that the page uses the short name.

openQuestions.question: The dataset document fsf-2024 groups the announcement post (bylined Anca Dragan, Helen King, Allan Dafoe) with the framework PDF (credited to Google DeepMind). Should the announcement become its own document record so that its bylines can carry authorship?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: split the announcement into a document of its own in a later correction, then admit Allan Dafoe on his research page as identity; until then hold him. Do not record the Acknowledgements’ “under the leadership of” as authorship.
